definitions.explanation: A face-to-face visit, especially to see someone in a hospital, prison, or other institution. Also used for formal meetings with officials or important figures.

examples.japanese: {面会|めんかい}{時間|じかん}は{午後|ごご}3{時|じ}までです。
{入院中|にゅういんちゅう}の{祖母|そぼ}に{面会|めんかい}しに{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to visit my grandmother in the hospital.

examples.japanese: {感染症|かんせんしょう}{対策|たいさく}のため、{面会|めんかい}は{一日|いちにち}一{組|くみ}までに{制限|せいげん}されている。
examples.english: Due to infection control measures, visits are limited to one group per day.

notes:
USAGE:
{面会|めんかい} is most commonly used for visiting someone in an institutional setting such as a hospital or prison. It has a more formal and structured nuance than a casual visit.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {面会|めんかい}する (to visit, to meet)
- {面会|めんかい}{時間|じかん} (visiting hours)
- {面会|めんかい}{謝絶|しゃぜつ} (no visitors allowed)
- {面会|めんかい}に{行|い}く (to go visit)
- {面会|めんかい}を{断|ことわ}る (to refuse a visit)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{見舞|みま}い focuses on visiting someone who is ill to wish them well, while {面会|めんかい} is the broader, more formal term for any institutional visit.
